title: Why Does Your Finger JUMP When You Close One Eye? 👁️
description:
Point at something across the room, then shut one eye, then the other. With one of them, your finger jumps. Each eye sees your finger from a slightly different spot, so when the two pictures disagree your brain aims with just one of them: your dominant eye, the boss. Shut the boss and you get the other eye's picture, and the finger jumps. Which eye is your boss? Left or right?

About two in three people have a right-eye boss, and it doesn't always match the hand you write with (roughly a third of right-handers are left-eyed). The other eye isn't idle: you need both for depth.
